title: Sales Enablement: Positioning & Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Jordan Reyes
body:
Summary:
This consolidated sales enablement doc provides repeatable positioning, competitive talking points, a recommended pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Use this as the canonical reference for AE & SE motions when qualifying and closing deals.

1) One-line & positioning statements
- One-liner (customer facing): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-effective LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- For engineering leaders: Move inference from an operational burden to a predictable, observable service — reduce per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs and compliance requirements.
- For platform teams: Provide standardized inference runtimes, rollout controls, and cost/leverage reporting across business units.

2) Messaging pillars (top 5)
- Production-grade performance: Guaranteed latency windows and throughput controls (hosted + Dedicated SLAs).
- Predictable economics: Cost levers (batching, cache, quantization) + unit economics dashboards.
- Deployment flexibility: Same API and operational tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem).
- Reliability with graceful degradation: Automatic routing/fallbacks to compatible model variants and regions.
- Developer experience: Quickstart SDKs, streaming responses, and model catalog with verified performance profiles.

3) Competitive brief (3 nearest competitor archetypes & talking points)
- General cloud AI platforms (big cloud provider managed endpoints)
  - Strengths: Tight cloud integration, single vendor for infra + model hosting.
  - Redwood differentiation: Platform-agnostic serving runtime with optimized kernels and cost controls; stronger tooling for canary rollouts, cache-aware batching, and per-route cost breakdowns.
  - Counterpoints: If asked about integration, emphasize our marketplace connectors and partner deployments for major cloud providers.

- LLM API-focused vendors (easy API access, curated models)
  - Strengths: Simpler onboarding and broad model access.
  - Redwood differentiation: We match simplicity but add production economics (dedicated capacity, autoscaling policies) and private deployment options for regulated customers.
  - Objection handling: For pilot customers who outgrow sandbox performance, propose a Dedicated trial to demonstrate throughput stability.

- Self-hosted inference/infrastructure vendors
  - Strengths: Full control and potentially lower long-term cost for massive scale.
  - Redwood differentiation: Reduce ops overhead with our orchestration, optimized runtime, and enterprise tooling (audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations) while enabling private deployments for isolation.
  - Close plan: Offer a migration assessment and an ROI analysis showing operational cost savings and time to market.

4) Recommended pitch deck (12 slides, concise flow)
- Slide 1: Title / Customer logo (if co-selling) + one-liner positioning.
- Slide 2: Why inference is hard (latency, cost, reliability, rollouts).
- Slide 3: Redwood value proposition (three bullets: performance, economics, flexibility).
- Slide 4: Product overview (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Slide 5: Architecture at a glance (serving runtime, smart routing, cache & batching).
- Slide 6: Performance benchmarks (representative latency & throughput for common models).
- Slide 7: Pricing & purchasing options (self-serve vs reserved capacity vs private licensing).
- Slide 8: Security & compliance (audit logging, KMS, VPC options).
- Slide 9: Customer examples / case study highlights.
- Slide 10: Deployment & rollout plan (POC -> pilot -> production).
- Slide 11: Support & SLAs (operational support tiers).
- Slide 12: Ask / next steps (trial, technical workshop).

5) Pricing guidance (talking points & example structures)
- Pricing models we sell:
  - Hosted (usage-based): per-token generation + per-embedding units. Typical starter rate guidance: $X per 1K generation tokens, $Y per 1K embedding units. (Use the pricing calculator: sales pricing sheet for current list rates.)
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual GPU pool commitments with an ingress/egress unit price for excess usage. Discount tiers typically at 25-45% vs equivalent hosted costs depending on term & committed throughput.
  - Private (enterprise licensing): platform fee + optional support & deployment professional services.
- Negotiation levers for AE/SEs: term length, committed throughput, overage caps, data residency & retention requirements, premium support SLAs.
- Quick example (discuss in calls only; give ballpark): For a mid-market SaaS customer with 20M tokens/month, Dedicated vs Hosted break-even often occurs in the 6-12 month window depending on batching and quantization choices. Use the ROI worksheet in the sales kit to produce a customer-specific analysis.

6) Case studies (concise customer narratives for prospect resonance)
- Case study A: Fintech SaaS — Fraud Triage API
  - Problem: High latency and cost on in-house LLM endpoints caused missed SLAs and escalating infra spend.
  - Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated with KV caching and model quantization profile; implemented prefix caching for common requests.
  - Outcome: 3x reduction in p99 latency for inference paths, 42% reduction in per-token cost, and a stable production SLA.

- Case study B: Healthcare enterprise — Private deployment (VPC)
  - Problem: Strict PHI controls and on-prem requirements prevented cloud LLM use.
  - Solution: Deployed Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS and audit logging; integrated with internal CI/CD for model rollouts.
  - Outcome: Achieved compliance requirements, reduced time to deploy new model versions from 4 weeks to 5 days, and enabled a pilot of clinical summarization workloads.

7) Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for sales & SE use)
- Q: Where is customer data stored and processed?
  - A: Hosted API processes data in the region selected by the customer; logs and analytics are stored in our secure object store with retention configurable per contract. For sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment options where data never leaves customer-controlled networks.

- Q: Do you provide encryption at rest and in transit?
  - A: Yes. TLS 1.2+ for in-transit and AES-256 for at-rest storage. For Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integrations.

- Q: How do you handle access control and auditability?
  - A: RBAC for console & API access, API keys with usage scopes, and a centralized audit log delivered to the customer SIEM or via secure export.

- Q: What compliance regimes do you support?
  - A: We support SOC 2 Type II evidence; HIPAA-ready controls are available via Private/Dedicated offerings and a BAAs. For EU customers, data residency and GDPR controls are available. See security and compliance pages for current certificates.

- Q: How do you protect model IP and customer prompts?
  - A: We segregate model artifacts, provide role separation for model onboarding, and can deploy models on dedicated hosts. Customer prompt data is treated as input; for regulated customers, data retention can be disabled and logs forwarded only to customer endpoints.

8) Demo checklist (SE playbook for a 45-minute technical demo)
1. Intro (5m): Objectives and success criteria.
2. Architecture walkthrough (10m): show runtime, routing, and deployment options.
3. Live demo (15m): Hosted API quickstart -> show streaming generation -> show embeddings + search example.
4. Observability (5m): Show token-level cost dashboard, latency heatmap, and rollout trace.
5. Roadmap & next steps (5m): POC plan, sample timelines.
6. Q&A & security deep dive (5m).

9) Objection handling (common closes)
- "We can self-host cheaper": Ask about ops headcount, time to production, and total cost of ownership (include quantized model maintenance). Offer an ROI assessment + pilot.
- "We need absolute data isolation": Recommend Private deployment and outline technical ownership model & timeline.
- "Latency is unacceptable": Show benchmark examples and propose a Dedicated trial with defined p99 latency targets.
